thread_title: [MNO] Starhub Mobile Discussion
post_text:
More StarHub 5G+ FAQs:
https://www.starhub.com/personal/support/article.html?id=uyu7jnAgiM5NdRhAt0jR79
2. How is StarHub's 5G+ different from 5G?
5G+ builds on regular 5G with added network capacity. You get up to 4x faster speeds, stronger connections in places like indoors, underground, and crowded environments, and a smoother, more consistent experience overall.
9. What are the benefits of 5G+ besides faster speed?
Beyond speed, 5G+ gives you stronger connections in places that are usually tricky for any network, like indoors, underground, and crowded environments. The result is a smoother, more consistent experience overall, not just a faster one.
10. Does 5G+ work while roaming overseas?
Not yet. 5G+ runs on 5G Standalone (SA) technology, and our roaming partners currently only support 5G Non-Standalone (NSA). While roaming, you'll stay connected on 5G NSA or 4G, depending on what's available in that country.
11. How do I get connected to StarHub 5G+?
You'll need three things: a 5G mobile plan, a 5G SIM or eSIM, and a supported 5G+ device
12. How will I know my device is connected to 5G+?
Your network indicator may vary depending on your device manufacturer and software version. For supported Android models, customers will see “5G+” beside network signal strength. E.g. Samsung Galaxy Fold8/Fold8 Ultra/Flip8 will display 5G+.
13. What happens if I'm temporarily unable to connect to the StarHub 5G+ network?
On instances where the 5G+ network is unavailable, you will automatically be switched to our 5G or 4G network to ensure you remain connected online. As soon as 5G+ network becomes accessible, you will automatically be reconnected back.
14. In what frequency band and spectrum(s) is StarHub running its 5G+ network on?
StarHub's 5G Standalone Access (SA) is deployed on 3.5GHz, 2.1GHz and 700MHz spectrum that allows us to enhance and expand our 5G coverage.
